items.reference:
Closed, Open, Half-Open
🔒 Closed: calls flow, failures counted
🚫 Open: refused instantly, no network call
🧪 Half-Open: one trial call decides the next state
Why: Half-Open probes recovery cheaply instead of reopening the floodgates blindly.
items.learnMore:
Why three states

Closed and Open alone would either never recover or flip back with a flood of traffic. Half-Open lets exactly one trial request measure recovery: success closes the circuit, failure reopens it and restarts the cooldown.

Common mistake

Thinking an Open breaker stays open forever, or that cooldown expiry means the dependency is healthy.

items.explanation: The trialInFlight flag admits a single probe, so a burst cannot hit a recovering dependency. A half-open failure reopens at once with a fresh openedAt, restarting the cooldown, while a success resets the count and closes the circuit.
items.reference:
The breaker state machine
🔒 Closed: count failures, open at threshold
🚫 Open: refuse until cooldown elapses
🧪 Half-Open: one trial; success closes, failure reopens
Why: time is passed in as now, so every transition is deterministic.
items.learnMore:
Three transitions, one trial

The only subtle parts are admitting exactly one half-open trial and restarting the cooldown when that trial fails. Both prevent bursts against a recovering dependency.

Common mistake

Letting every caller through the moment the cooldown ends, or forgetting that a failed trial reopens immediately.
items.reflection: A state machine with a single probe is a pattern for any cautious restart. Where else would you retry a risky action once, small, before committing to it fully?
